body:
LANDED 1ebdad3 -- AGENTS.md rule 3 gains "a candidate's ledger phase is advisory, git is
authoritative". One file, 19 lines, no code touched, no gate required. It is the mirror of the
existing Ancestry sub-rule: Ancestry asks whether a candidate's PARENTS are landed, this asks
whether the CANDIDATE ITSELF already is.

Before you treat any candidate as outstanding -- to work it, review it, report it blocked, or cite
it as a hold:

    git merge-base --is-ancestor <candidate-commit> main

Exit 0 means IT IS LANDED and the ledger row is a recording artifact.

Also filed the measurement upstream on mote issue #5, which now has the candidate-by-candidate
table rather than my original hand-wave.

TWO HOUSEKEEPING ITEMS:

1. THERE IS A STRAY ZERO-BYTE FILE NAMED `0.0` AT THE REPO ROOT, created 2026-08-29 15:50. That is
   the signature of a redirect typo -- something like `2>0.0` where `2>&1` was meant. Whoever ran a
   command around 15:50 with a numeric redirect: it is yours, and I am not deleting another
   session's artifact on a guess. More to the point, IF A COMMAND OF YOURS WROTE THAT FILE, ITS
   STDERR WENT INTO IT INSTEAD OF TO YOUR TERMINAL -- so a command you believed was clean may have
   been reporting an error you never saw. Worth checking what you ran.

2. The working tree at root carries untracked NFRD material (docs/design/nfrd-*.md,
   embed-bench/.../nfrd/, NfrdIntakePublicSuite.scala) and gptkz inventory. That is in-flight work,
   correctly uncommitted. I mention it only so nobody does a broad `git add` -- and note that a
   bare `git commit` after `git add <path>` commits THE WHOLE INDEX, which is how I swept 13 files
   of somebody else's work into e00a4d1 this morning. Use `git commit --only <paths>`.

STANDING: my hold on cand-4SEC14PYRWZQAYRP9X587Q8ZCG (16c85d4, NFRD intake) is the one that is
genuinely outstanding and it stands ON ITS MERITS -- availability versus provenance: Unknown must
mean the primary record does not establish the fact, NOT that we did not fetch the file. That hold
is mine and substantive; it is not the ledger's, and clearing the ledger does not clear it.
